transcript:
Header:
- Date: 2026-06-10
- Time: 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~46 minutes
- Location: Zoom call
- Recording: yes

Summary (auto):
Silverpine is evaluating an exit from their current Anthropic/OpenAI mix to reduce per-token costs and get more predictable latency for peak trading-hours style workloads. Primary constraints: low tail latency for short responses, SOC2/ISO requirements, VPC option for sensitive logs, and ability to run parity evals (RAG + streaming + function calls). They asked about Redwood hosted vs Dedicated vs Private and compatibility with their vLLM/TGI-based infra. Next steps agreed: send security docs, run benchmarks, and provide pricing scenarios.

Topics:
- Current stack and pain points
- Model compatibility and eval parity (TGI, vLLM)
- Hosting options: hosted vs dedicated vs private
- Security, compliance, and network requirements
- Benchmarks and pilot scope

Attendees and quick intros (0:00)\[00:00:05\] Alex Rivera (Redwood AE): "Hey everyone, Alex here, I'm the AE on the account, I'll kick us off."
\[00:00:12\] Ravi Patel (CTO, Silverpine): "Ravi, hi, thanks for making time. We're in a kind of transition — want to explore tradeoffs."
\[00:00:20\] Marta Liang (SE, Redwood): "Marta, I'm the systems SE, I'll get into performance and hosting questions."
\[00:00:27\] Sophie Cole (ML Eng): "Sophie — I run our inference stack, mostly vLLM and a TGI wrapper."
\[00:00:32\] Marcus Dunn (Infra): "Marcus — infra and SRE."
\[00:00:35\] Ellen Park (Head of Sec): "Ellen — security and compliance."

Start of discovery (0:40)\[00:00:40\] Alex: "Can you tell us what you're running today and what the trigger is for looking?"
\[00:00:45\] Ravi: "Sure. We're currently hybrid — a mix. For high-sensitivity calls we use Anthropic through Azure OpenAI for some routing. For most user-facing generation we call OpenAI gpt-4 and have a vLLM fleet for lower latency, on prem. Cost spiked Q1 and we hit some weird tail-latency during peak trading windows, so throughput isn't predictable. Also procurement wants fewer vendor lock-ins. So looking at options: hosted Redwood API, Redwood Dedicated reserved pools, or full Private deployment in our VPC/on-prem. Main goals: comparable quality, predictable cost, and security controls."
\[00:01:30\] Sophie: "To add, we use TGI as a fronting layer in some experiments — mainly for batching and custom tokenization. Can Redwood run models compiled via TGI or vLLM replays?"

Model compatibility & eval parity (1:20)\[00:01:20\] Marta: "Short answer: yes, we onboard models and have compatibility layers. There are edge cases around custom kernels and operator-level differences that can affect eval parity, especially for fine-tuned checkpoints and bits-and-bytes quantization. Can you describe the exact models and any custom ops?"
\[00:01:38\] Sophie: "We run a mixture: Mistral-like open weights, a few LoRA-tuned checkpoints, and some 4-bit quantized variants using bitsandbytes. We also heavily rely on KV cache persistence for chat sessions — stateful sessions are critical."
\[00:01:55\] Marta: "We support bnb/4-bit quant profiles and have a pipeline to validate outputs vs a golden test set during onboarding. Two caveats: (1) some LoRA adapters that modify attention mechanisms need special handling, (2) operator-level differences can cause minor tokenization or spacing differences that change eval scores — we run parity evaluations with your test prompts to quantify delta."
\[00:02:18\] Sophie: "Okay makes sense. For our parity bar, we need within 2% BLEU/ROUGE-ish on our prompts and no regression in hallucination rate by more than 1%."
\[00:02:27\] Alex: "We can commit to a formal parity run and share a baseline report. We'll also log diffs so your team can triage model-specific mismatches."

Hosting modes and tradeoffs (5:15)\[00:05:15\] Alex: "Let's talk tradeoffs quickly: Hosted API gives fastest time to value — we manage everything, simple API, streaming, function calling, token-level costs. Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools, predictable throughput, and isolation. Private lets you host in VPC or on-prem with customer-managed keys and air-gap options. Where do you land on control vs ops?"
\[00:05:36\] Marcus: "Ops-wise we prefer to own networking and keys. But we also don't want to babysit CUDA drivers. Dedicated seems attractive — we could have a tenancy with predictable SLAs but still keep some control."
\[00:05:50\] Ellen: "From sec angle, Private with customer KMS and SOC2 plus audit logs is ideal, but procurement will object to the engineering time and the cost. If Dedicated supports SAML and our KMS it's probably acceptable."
\[00:06:05\] Alex: "On Dedicated we support VPC peering and bring-your-own-KMS for encryption-at-rest keys. Private is the full control option but adds deployment time. Hosted can be bolstered with VPC egress and strict log retention policies for certain accounts."

Performance specifics and SLOs (8:00)\[00:08:00\] Sophie: "Latency: 95th percentile for single-turn responses needs to be under 120ms for small prompts; under 300ms for multi-step plugin-ish flows. Can Redwood guarantee tail latency?"
\[00:08:15\] Jonah (SE): "We publish observed tails per-model and can set SLOs depending on deployment mode. Dedicated gives the tightest tail because you get reserved pools and we can set batch sizes and pre-warm KV caches. Hosted relies on service-wide autoscaling; in practice we hit similar tails but Dedicated is definitely more predictable."
\[00:08:34\] Marcus: "How does prefix/KV caching work? We have long-lived sessions — caching saves tokens and CPU."
\[00:08:40\] Marta: "We provide automatic KV cache preservation for session affinity in Dedicated and Private; for Hosted we offer token-level prefix cache with TTLs and a cache warming API. We also support pinned caches for enterprise customers during pilots."

Security and compliance deep dive (12:45)\[00:12:45\] Ellen: "We need SOC2 Type II, ISO27001, SSO via SAML / Okta, RBAC, and audit log export to our SIEM. Data residency: logs must be retained per our policy and PII redaction is required for stored traces."
\[00:13:05\] Alex: "We have SOC2 and ISO docs; Dedicated and Private both support SAML SSO and fine-grained RBAC. For audit logs, we can stream to your SIEM or provide daily exports. We also offer optional redaction at ingestion and redaction hooks for custom PII rules."
\[00:13:28\] Ellen: "KMS integration — can we bring our own keys / HSM?"
\[00:13:33\] Marta: "Yes: Dedicated and Private both support BYOK via KMS, and Private supports direct HSM connections for air-gapped setups."

Vendor exit mechanics and contract questions (16:30)\[00:16:30\] Ravi: "We have a one-year contract with OpenAI through our enterprise agreement; switching will be phased. What's the minimal friction path? How do you handle API compatibility and session migration?"
\[00:16:42\] Alex: "We can adopt an adapter approach: keep the same prompt patterns and wrap requests through a compatibility layer during pilot. For sessions we can extract KV cache snapshots where possible and replay into Redwood runtime for parity checks. We'll work with your SREs to create a staged cutover: shadow traffic, then canary, then full migration."
\[00:17:05\] Sophie: "Shadowing is important. Also, can Redwood front TGI/vLLM on the backend so we keep our custom batching?"
\[00:17:12\] Marta: "We can route to a customer-managed backend in Private mode. For Hosted/Dedicated we can provide a compatibility layer that mimics TGI behavior (tokenization, batching), but some of your custom gRPC hooks may need adapter work."

Cost comparison and pricing model (19:50)\[00:19:50\] Alex: "High level: Hosted is per-token with volume tiers and discounting; Dedicated is reserved monthly for GPU pools with overage and burst; Private is licensing plus infra. We can build a cost model using your QPS and token distribution."
\[00:20:05\] Marcus: "We want to understand unit economics vs our current spend with OpenAI and Anthropic. Also curious about quantization options to reduce GPU memory and cost."
\[00:20:14\] Alex: "We support quantized execution profiles; our Optimize product will recommend 4-bit/8-bit profiles and expected cost delta. We'll share a spreadsheet comparing per-token + infra amortized costs across modes."

Benchmarks and pilot plan (23:00)\[00:23:00\] Marta: "Suggested pilot: 2-week parity run. Stage 1: offline eval of your prompt set on our test cluster — compare output metrics. Stage 2: small live shadow with 1% traffic to measure tail latency and end-to-end error rates. Stage 3: 72-hour canary at 10-20% traffic. We'll capture token counts and trace sampling."
\[00:23:25\] Sophie: "What do you need from us?"
\[00:23:28\] Marta: "Sample prompt set, golden outputs, QPS profile, model list, and any LoRA adapters or calibration steps."
\[00:23:33\] Ravi: "We'll produce that, but need non-disclosure assurances — can we have a mutual NDA?"
\[00:23:39\] Alex: "Yes, we'll send a standard mutual NDA; we also have a data processing addendum for pilot data."

Objections and back-and-forth (27:40)\[00:27:40\] Ellen: "Procurement will push back on Private because of ops cost. What's the expected timeline to get Private live?"
\[00:27:47\] Jonah: "Private deployments typically take 8-12 weeks end-to-end for customer-managed air-gapped installs depending on site approvals. Dedicated can be provisioned in 2-4 weeks."
\[00:27:58\] Marcus: "If we go Dedicated, how much work on our side to integrate KMS and SSO?"
\[00:28:04\] Marta: "Usually 1-2 weeks for SAML and KMS integration testing; we provide a runbook and dedicated onboarding SE for enterprise deals."

Transcript noise / misc (31:10)\[00:31:10\] Speaker 1 (unlabeled): "uhh — sorry, can you repeat how you do prefix caching? I kinda missed it"
\[00:31:15\] Marta: "Sure — we persist KV caches per-session id with optional sticky routing. For Dedicated you can pin caches to a GPU slice. On Hosted we keep TTLs and warm caches on demand."

Legal & procurement checklist (34:00)\[00:34:00\] Alex: "We'll include contract templates: SOC2 attestation, DPA, SLAs, and an enterprise addendum for Dedicated/Private. Any specific redlines you expect?"
\[00:34:12\] Ravi: "Termination clauses and indemnity, plus data residency clauses for EU — some of our traffic is EU-only."
\[00:34:20\] Alex: "Noted. We'll surface EU-region hosting options and regional data residency in the contract."

Wrap-up and recap (39:10)\[00:39:10\] Alex: "Recap: (1) You will share sample prompts & QPS, (2) We'll send SOC2/ISO docs + NDA, (3) Martha — sorry Marta — will draft benchmark plan, (4) We'll share pricing for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private and a cost-model spreadsheet, (5) Tentative pilot window next week if NDA signed."
\[00:39:38\] Ravi: "Sounds good. One more question: what's Redwood's typical SLA for Dedicated?"
\[00:39:44\] Alex: "We offer 99.9% uptime SLAs for Dedicated with latency SLOs tied to instance sizing; details in the SLA pack."
\[00:39:52\] Ellen: "And audit logs — are they tamper-evident?"
\[00:39:56\] Marta: "We can stream logs with signed checksums and integrate with your SIEM; Private has the most control for tamper-evidence."

Closing (45:00)\[00:45:00\] Alex: "Thanks everyone — we'll follow up via email with the docs and send a calendar invite for the benchmark kickoff. Any final notes?"
\[00:45:12\] Sophie: "Appreciate it. We'll try to get the prompt set over by Friday. Also, small ask — can you include example curl commands for function calls and streaming?"
\[00:45:24\] Alex: "Yep, we'll include examples and a reference snippet for TGI adapter behavior."
